correctness.rationale: The geometric-series polynomial identity is checked at every n including n=1; unitary dilation supplies a sharp universal upper bound. A wandering vector constructs explicitly normalized weak-null approximate eigenvectors with residual sqrt(2/L), making every compact perturbation at least the circle-symbol maximum. Log-derivative strict negativity excludes other lobes and proves the unique global maximum. Uniform Taylor expansion near a nondegenerate limiting root yields the \(n^{-2}\) coefficient and O(\(n^{-4}\)) remainder. The Hilbert mean-ergodic theorem gives strong convergence but no norm convergence. Numerical root values confirm, but do not establish, the infinite statements.

value.rationale: Natural question at the interface of quantitative mean ergodic theory and noncompactness: one asks how far consecutive dyadic averages remain apart after strong convergence and under finite-rank/compact perturbations. The theorem settles that operator-ideal invariant sharply for every nonunitary Hilbert isometry, provides a unique exact finite-scale frequency and a nontrivial positive \(n^{-2}\) correction, and makes the persistent Calkin obstruction explicit. This is not a relabeling or an arbitrary parameter slice: it quantifies an intrinsic oscillation invisible to fixed-vector convergence rates.
